Write the conclusion (effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective) with evidence references.
Have an independent reviewer who performed none of the sampled re-performance sign the workpaper.
Report the conclusion to the Market Conduct / Consumer Compliance Manager and file the workpaper in the evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion exists and results are reported to the Market Conduct / Consumer Compliance Manager.

Where an updated address is found, correct the policy record and re-dispatch the notice.
Where no updated contact is found, escalate to the Policy Administrator for outbound phone contact before the statutory deadline passes.
checklist.done: every bad-address delivery is either corrected and re-dispatched, or escalated for phone contact before the deadline.

checklist.step: Run the daily batch-exception report
actions: Each morning, review the batch-exception report for jobs that failed to run, ran short, or errored on a subset of policies.
Re-run any failed or short job the same day and confirm the reconciled count on re-run.
Escalate any exception that cannot be cleared same-day to the Head of Compliance.
checklist.done: the daily exception report is reviewed with same-day re-run or escalation for every exception.

checklist.step: Monitor for policies approaching their statutory deadline without a generated notice
actions: Run a daily query for policies within 5 days of their statutory notice deadline with no generated notice on file.
Manually trigger notice generation for any policy the query surfaces.
Log the manual trigger and its cause on the notice log.
checklist.done: no policy reaches its statutory deadline without either an automated or a manually triggered notice, logged either way.

checklist.step: Log any late-generated or undelivered notice as an exception
actions: Raise a tracker issue for any notice generated or dispatched after its statutory lead time.
Document the root cause (batch failure, bad address, late eligibility flag) and the cure taken.
Route to the Market Conduct / Consumer Compliance Manager for sign-off.
checklist.done: every late or undelivered notice is logged with a documented cause and cure, signed off by the Market Conduct / Consumer Compliance Manager.

checklist.step: Reconcile the monthly notice log to the policy lifecycle events
actions: At month end, pull every renewal, non-renewal and new-business event from the policy administration system for the month.
Confirm each event has a corresponding notice-log entry with a generation and dispatch timestamp.
List any event missing a notice-log entry as an exception for same-week remediation.
checklist.done: every lifecycle event for the month is matched to a notice-log entry, with gaps remediated the same week.

checklist.step: Verify the notice content matches the approved template
actions: Pull 10 generated notices at random from the month's batch and compare rendered content to the currently approved form-library template.
Confirm merge fields populated correctly (coverage limits, effective dates, insured name/address).
Escalate any rendering defect to the Policy Admin Ops Lead for immediate correction.
checklist.done: 10 sampled notices match the approved template with correct merge-field population, and any defect is escalated immediately.

checklist.step: Brief Market Conduct on notice-delivery performance
actions: Summarize monthly generation volume, exception count and cure rate.
Present the summary to the Market Conduct / Consumer Compliance Manager.
Record any directed process improvement.
checklist.done: the Market Conduct / Consumer Compliance Manager has received the monthly notice-delivery performance summary.

checklist.step: Update the batch schedule for any Manual timing change
actions: Monitor for NFIP Flood Insurance Manual updates that change notice lead-time requirements.
Redline the batch schedule configuration and route it for Head of Compliance approval.
Test the updated schedule in non-production before promoting to production.
checklist.done: the batch schedule reflects the latest Manual timing requirement, approved and tested before production promotion.

checklist.step: Test disaster-recovery failover for the notice batch process
actions: Confirm the correspondence batch engine is included in the annual DR test scope.
Verify notices due during a simulated outage window are queued and generated once systems recover, without exceeding the statutory deadline.
Document the DR test result for the notice batch process.
checklist.done: the annual DR test confirms notice generation resumes without breaching statutory deadlines, documented in the DR test record.

checklist.step: Audit the delivery-preference data quality
actions: Quarterly, sample policies for a valid mailing address or e-delivery consent on file.
Flag policies with incomplete delivery-preference data to the Correspondence Clerk for outreach.
Track the completion rate of outreach follow-up.
checklist.done: a quarterly delivery-preference data-quality sample is run with outreach tracked to completion.

checklist.step: Retain the notice-delivery evidence
actions: Move the notice log, generation logs, delivery/bounce reports and exception resolutions into the compliance evidence repository under the month.
Apply the 7-year retention label and confirm searchability by policy number and notice type.
Confirm the month is closed out in the notice log index.
checklist.done: notice-delivery evidence is filed, retention-labelled, searchable by policy and notice type, and the month is closed out.

testing.step: Build the population of statutory notices due in the test period
actions: Independently query the policy administration system for every renewal, non-renewal and new-business event in the test month.
Reconcile the count to the notice log's lifecycle-event reconciliation for the same month.
Resolve any unreconciled event before sampling.
testing.done: the population of due notices is reconciled to the notice log with no unresolved gaps.

testing.step: Select the sample and document the selection method
actions: Take 100% of notices logged as an exception (late, bad address, undelivered) in the month.
Take 25 additional notices at random (seeded, reproducible) from the on-time population.
Record the seed and population size in the workpaper.
testing.done: the sample covers all exceptions plus 25 random on-time notices, documented in the workpaper.

testing.step: Recompute generation timing against the statutory lead time
actions: For each sampled notice, pull the statutory lead-time requirement from the current NFIP Flood Insurance Manual.
Recompute the required generation window from the triggering event date and compare to the actual generation timestamp on the notice log.
Flag any notice generated outside the required window as an exception.
testing.done: generation timing is independently recomputed and compared for every sampled notice.

testing.step: Trace dispatch and delivery confirmation on the sample
actions: Pull the dispatch confirmation (vendor batch id or e-delivery send id) for each sampled notice.
Confirm delivery/bounce report status and, for any bounce, confirm a re-delivery task was opened and closed with a cure.
Flag any notice without a dispatch confirmation or an unresolved bounce as an exception.
testing.done: dispatch and delivery status are independently traced for the sample with unresolved bounces flagged.

testing.step: Independently compare notice content to the approved template
actions: Open each sampled notice's rendered document and the approved form-library template version in force on the generation date.
Compare content and merge-field population field by field.
Flag any content mismatch or merge-field error as an exception.
testing.done: notice content is independently compared to the approved template for every sampled notice.

testing.step: Re-perform the manual-trigger monitoring check
actions: Independently query for any policy in the test month that reached its statutory deadline with no notice-log entry.
Compare to the operational team's daily monitoring query results for the same period.
Flag any policy the independent query finds that the operational monitoring missed.
testing.done: the manual-trigger monitoring control is independently re-performed with any missed policy flagged.

testing.step: Verify exception resolution and sign-off
actions: Pull every exception logged for the sampled notices from the tracker.
Confirm the documented cure was actually applied (address corrected, notice re-sent, escalation resolved).
Flag any exception without a confirmed cure as still open.
testing.done: logged exceptions are traced to a confirmed cure or flagged as still open.

testing.step: Verify retention labelling and searchability
actions: Open the compliance evidence repository entry for the test month.
Confirm the 7-year retention label is applied and records are searchable by policy number and notice type.
Flag any missing or mislabelled record as an exception.
testing.done: retention labelling and searchability are confirmed for the test month's evidence.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a tracker issue per exception with the policy number, notice type and what failed.
Assign a root cause and an owner, and set a remediation date.
Carry unresolved exceptions into the next month's test as mandatory retest items.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, root cause, owner, remediation date and retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute the exception rate for the month and compare to the zero-late-notice threshold.
Write the conclusion (effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective) with evidence references.
Have an independent reviewer who performed none of the sampled re-performance sign the workpaper.
Report the conclusion to the Head of Compliance and file the workpaper in the evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion exists and results are reported to the Head of Compliance.
